answer: Found and fixed the SUID vulnerability. The `/usr/bin/find` binary had an unauthorized SUID bit set (`-rwsr-xr-x`), which could allow users to read files they shouldn't have access to (e.g., `find /etc/shadow` would run as root and display the file). Fixed it by removing the SUID bit with `chmod u-s /usr/bin/find`, resulting in normal permissions (`-rwxr-xr-x`).
